user_feedback: GD-SB depth was too high/lower than the valve and would increase strain through elevation effect.
High-strain marker for pipeline peak strain was anchored to a GD-SB corner instead of the pipeline near the connector.
Connector on the header line was added at a valve end node instead of a GD-TP connector landing, indicating EDAS was not referred.
root_cause: The layout workflow used generic/default support geometry and a simplified connector representation after the design response, rather than re-entering EDAS/EDIKB gates before plotting. Existing connector landing knowledge existed, but the inline-valve base depth did not have a deterministic elevation/clearance gate.
implemented_rules: For GD-VLV protected by GD-SB, compute valve lower envelope and check GD-SB bottom clearance against a bounded clearance allowance.
For GD-VLV protected by GD-SB, check connector/elevation arm abs(P_vt) against a bounded maximum unless explicit EDIKB evidence justifies a larger value.
For complete/review plots, connector load paths must be represented by GD-Con parts landing on GD-TP/GD-TT/GD-PIP/GD-BOSS connector hosts, not directly on GD-VLV or plain header nodes.
Pipeline peak strain annotations must use pipeline/model-coordinate anchors near the connector or load-transfer region, and uncertainty must be stated if the exact location is not evidenced.
validation: Unit regression added for over-deep versus fitted GD-SB valve-base geometry gate.
Corrected Test 02 layout to use fitted GD-SB dimensions, GD-TP pipe landing bodies, GD-Con connector objects, and pipeline-anchored high-strain annotation.
